$comment: PROPOSAL — NOT canonical, NOT vendored into the suite, NOT SHA-pinned, NOT adopted. Wire-contract draft for STATION events: a radio stream a user follows in radio-scan, published so others can discover and follow it. Lives in the external repo github.com/macos-node/radio-scan for TESTING ONLY. Kinds are locked provisionally against the suite's used set (1063/4550/27235/30000/31237/31238/31239): station.v1 = 31241, its sibling airplay.v1 = 31240 — both free, contiguous with the suite's 31237-31239 block. No .sha256 pin and no freeze governance apply until this is proposed to merge into the suite (ndisc/schema). Design rationale: docs/radio-scan-buildmap-2026-07-28.md and schema/airplay-design-2026-07-28.md.
canonicalHome: macos-node/radio-scan — schema/station.v1.json (proposal; not yet in ndisc/schema)

authority.model: per-publisher key — any pubkey publishes its OWN followed-stations set; there is no single owner or gate. Mirrors clip.v1's per-publisher model, not feed.v1's single-owner root.
authority.note: Cross-user 'who else follows this stream' filters on the stream URL via the single-letter #r tag, not on the per-author addressable coordinate.

station.class: addressable — re-publishing the same d-tag replaces in place (edit metadata, no event spam)
station.kindRationale: A followed station is a small, editable, per-user record — the addressable form fits (like release.v2 / feed.v1). 31241 sits contiguous with the suite's 31237-31239 block and is unused across the suite.
station.content: Optional human description of the station (plain text).
station.writtenBy: radio-scan (the L2 suite bridge), signed with the owner nsec from the OS keyring — the same key as ndisc/ntree/nsmpl (one person = one npub).

d.note: Derived from the STREAM URL, never from the station's name: `airplay:station:` + the first 16 hex of SHA-256 of the canonical URL. Canonicalization is pinned with conformance vectors in station-address.vectors.json and a publisher MUST pass them — two publishers disagreeing on a default port or a Shoutcast ';' would mint two addresses for one stream. Name-derived slugs did exactly that: one Acid Jazz mount became `acid-jazz`, `acid-jazz-2`, `acid-j` and `aj` across devices, all retracted 2026-08-19. A content-derived address is replaceable by construction, so the same stream followed on two devices is one event. KNOWN LIMIT: stable only while the URL is — a mount that moves host re-addresses, and stations have no publisher-stated identity (icy-name is a banner) to fall back on the way shows use podcast:guid. Decision #11.

name.note: Human display name of the station.

r.note: The direct stream URL (the mount, e.g. http://host:8000/mount). Single-letter tag so it is RELAY-FILTERABLE (#r) — the cross-user station identity: 'all stations / airplay for this URL' is a #r filter. Resolve playlist wrappers (.m3u/.pls/.xspf) to the real mount before publishing.

fmt.note: Advertised content-type, e.g. audio/aacp — from the stream's icy headers (radio-scan writes station_info.txt).

br.note: Advertised bitrate in kbps, integer as string, e.g. "320".

t.note: Genre / topic slug(s), lowercased (#t filterable). Align with the suite's genre slugs where they fit; free tags otherwise.

alt.note: NIP-31 human-readable fallback for generic clients.

station.rule: Consumers MUST require only d + name + r structurally; every descriptive tag (fmt/br/server/t) is optional. A station with no descriptive tags is still valid — it is a bare 'I follow this URL' record.

ownStations.note: Rebuild the user's own followed-station set from the relays (relay = truth, local = cache).

stationFollowers.note: Cross-user discovery: everyone who follows a given stream URL.

relatedContracts.airplay.v1: schema/airplay.v1.json — an observation references its station by both the #r URL (cross-user) and, optionally, this event's addressable `a` coordinate (own-hydrate).
relatedContracts.shared-registry: A curated shared station list can reuse the suite's kind:30000 (NIP-51 set, d=airplay:stations) + kind:4550 sign-off, exactly as the contributor registry does — out of scope for this file.

changePolicy: PROPOSAL — free to edit; no SHA pin, no coordinated-wave governance yet. If/when proposed to merge into the suite, it adopts the suite discipline (SHA-pin at the authority, additive-only after freeze, kind confirmed unused, coordinated re-vendor across consumers) — see clip.v1.json for the model.
